loop.top3_why: Candidate A uses a weighted pooled meta‑model that learns weights from a gradient‑boosted model trained across many other series. This approach is robust to the unstable model ranking observed in the diagnosis (Kendall tau –0.177) and to the high variance of weight estimation with only three validation windows. Its per‑window performance, while more variable than the plain mean, still stays within the overall best range and the overall score is the lowest among the three candidates. The weighted meta‑model has shown strong generalisation in the dataset card (weighted w=w1 is the best strategy overall).
loop.top3_why_not: Candidate B (plain mean) is stable but its validation score is noticeably higher (worse) and it does not exploit the information that some models are consistently better. Candidate C (DTW barycenter) has a slightly higher score than A and its per‑window errors are less consistent; the DTW barycenter is more sensitive to outliers and does not benefit from the strong trend dominance of this series. Therefore A is preferred over B and C.
